feedback.worked_solution:
First, we factor the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}\cdot {7}^{x}+6\cdot {7}^{x} & =-11x\cdot {7}^{x} \\ 3{x}^{2}\cdot {7}^{x}+11x\cdot {7}^{x}+6\cdot {7}^{x}+ & =0 \\ (3{x}^{2}+11x+6)\cdot {7}^{x} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

We can now apply the zero product property, which states that $ab=0$ if and only if $a=0$ or $b=0.$ This gives us two equations,

$$
3{x}^{2}+11x+6=0\,\text{and}\,{7}^{x}=0.
$$

We now solve each of these equations separately.

- The equation $3{x}^{2}+11x+6=0$ can be factored as

$$
(3x+2)(x+3)=0,
$$

which leads to the solutions $x=-3,-\frac{2}{3}.$

- The equation ${7}^{x}=0$ has no solutions because ${7}^{x}$ is positive for every real number $x.$

Therefore, in ascending order, the original equation has the solutions 

$$
x=-3\,\text{and}\,x=-\frac{2}{3}.
$$
